reason: The pictures show that the light-sensitive cells and retinal nerve cells belong in connected layers, so I can start the lining directly.
expectation: The cells will form a light-sensitive lining that passes signals toward the eye's outgoing fibres.

alternatives.reason: The clear fronts also fit the eye walls, so I could start the focusing parts instead.

effect: The light-sensitive cells and nerve cells made retinas, completing the lining goal. The eyes still need their focusing parts and connections.
reaction: The retina label makes the lining's name clearer.
reason: The corneas are transparent fronts, and the eye walls have matching clear-front slots.
expectation: The corneas will fit onto the fronts of the eye walls.

effect: The corneas are fitted and bend incoming light; the lenses and light controls still need fitting.
reaction: The bending-light picture makes the corneas' role clearer.
reason: The eye walls have a focusing-lens slot, and the lenses also bend light.
expectation: The lenses will fit inside the eye walls as another focusing part.

effect: The lenses are fitted behind the fronts, and their different shapes bend light by different amounts.
reaction: The comparison makes the lenses' focusing role clearer.
reason: The irises surround the pupil openings, so they fit the remaining light-control slot.
expectation: The irises will fit into the eye walls and control the openings that admit light.

effect: The irises complete the focusing parts, with pupil openings admitting different amounts of light.
reaction: The comparison makes the irises' role clear.
reason: The retinas are the light-sensitive linings, so they should fit inside the completed eye walls.
expectation: The retinas will join the focusing parts to form eyes that can detect incoming light.

effect: The retinas now sit behind the focusing parts, where incoming light reaches them. The eyes still need connections and moving muscles.
reaction: The picture makes the path of light through the eye clearer.
reason: The visual pathways lead from the back of the eyes toward the brain, so they are a clear next connection.

choice.combine: Eyes with focusing parts and retinas

expectation: The visual pathways will connect the eyes to a route toward the brain.

effect: The eyes now have visual pathways carrying signals away from them. They still need their moving muscles and connection to the body.
reaction: The signal arrows make the outgoing route clearer.
reason: The eye-moving muscles and nerves are pictured around the eyes, so they should attach to the prepared eyes.
expectation: The muscles and nerves will join the eyes so they can move.

alternatives.reason: I could try connecting the eyes to the body first, but the muscles also need attaching.

effect: The eyes now have moving muscles and nerves as well as visual pathways; they still need to connect to the body.
reaction: The opposing arrows show how the muscles pull the eyes.
reason: The visual pathways and muscle nerves lead toward the brain, so the prepared eyes should connect to the body.

choice.combine: Eyes with pathways and moving muscles

expectation: The eyes and their muscles will connect to the body's brain and nerves.

effect: The eyes and their muscles are connected to the body, completing the chapter. The final picture distinguishes light entering the eyes from nerve signals reaching the brain.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate parts become a body that can turn its eyes toward a face.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the retinas to the focusing parts was most worthwhile: it brought the separate projects together and showed the path light takes to the lining.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the three parts into the eye walls was a little repetitive, although the pictures explained each part’s job.

surprise.text: The comparison showing that flatter and rounder lenses bend light by different amounts made their focusing role clearer.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary. The slots and pictures made the fittings understandable, though they left little uncertainty about the pairings.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter: putting the eye together and following light toward signals was clear and satisfying, though I would hope for some less predictable choices.
